name: manual_57abee
claim: Python sqlite3.Connection as a context manager never closes the connection. Except when Python 3.12+ autocommit=True (where it does nothing), it commits on normal exit or rolls back on exception only if a transaction is open; with no open transaction it does nothing. In Python 3.11, isolation_level=None disables implicit transaction opening but an explicit BEGIN can still open one. Preserve both transaction and close semantics with contextlib.closing outside the transaction context (with closing(connection) as conn: with conn: ...), or a helper that commits or rolls back before finally closing. Test unclosed connections with ResourceWarning as an error on Python 3.13+ and an explicit leak assertion on older supported Python versions.

decisions.notes: Exact CPython context-manager behavior requires a final append-only refinement: isolation_level=None and autocommit=True are not equivalent; connection closing guidance and versioned leak-test advice remain unchanged.
